fullPassage: [P01] A problem that is shared with all methods for storing information about species distributions is that of information retrieval. In particular, computer databases and the World Wide Web are making information ever more accessible, but is that a problem? There are advantages and disadvantages in making information about species distributions openly available. In some cases, the more people that can access the information the better. For example, if planners have access to that information they may avoid the development of sites where rare species of plants and animals occur. Ecologists may use information in the design of ecological restoration projects. Land owners also may use information about species distributions in the design of farm management plans to identify areas most suitable for soil and water conservation. Scientists may be able to use the information that is available to provide ecological explanations for observed distribution patterns. However, access to information about the distribution of some species may have disadvantages. For example, information about the distribution of rare or threatened species may be used by people wanting to collect those species and as a result populations may become extinct. Populations of some species may be destroyed simply as a result of people visiting the site where the species occur, particularly those species that survive in fragile environments. [P02] Philosophical and historical research are the best examples of the confusion from which we suffer as to what constitutes research in the first place. In one sense research is an activity—the basic activity of science. Is philosophy science? Is history science? University philosophy and history departments are not included among the science departments in that philosophical and historical scholarship are considered to be essential in the humanities or social studies. Yet there are "Arts and Sciences" divisions that include them, even if, strictly speaking, they are neither art nor science. I have no particular interest in this confusion except that it makes apparent the association of the word "science" with the classical Newtonian assumptions that the universe is completely objective; science therefore is and must be completely objective; and anything not completely objective is, ipso facto, not science. Those assumptions are no longer valid even in the so-called hard sciences. While it may take several generations for these conceptual dilemmas to be worked out, we can begin to move in the direction of solutions by being more flexible in our definition of science. We should recognize that if scientific method is strictly conceived as being limited to experiments it is exemplary of the total scientific endeavor only under the narrowest, most regressive point of view. The experiment itself has been so thoroughly reassessed that we are no longer sure how to use it. So it would seem reasonable to conceive science as an endeavor, carried out in a great variety of ways, to achieve conceptual clarity about ourselves and our world. That permits philosophy and history to be part of the endeavor while also honoring the distinctions between science and those fields clearly not science, such as art and religion.

det.analysis: 본문 첫 문장 'A problem that is shared with all methods for storing information about species distributions is that of information retrieval' — 모든 저장 방식이 공유하는 문제 = information retrieval(정보 검색). 저장된 정보를 다시 꺼내는 일의 문제
det.tip: information retrieval = 정보 검색. 저장(storing)의 반대 과정.

questions.passage: [P01] A problem that is shared with all methods for storing information about species distributions is that of information retrieval. In particular, computer databases and the World Wide Web are making information ever more accessible, but is that a problem? There are advantages and disadvantages in making information about species distributions openly available. In some cases, the more people that can access the information the better. For example, if planners have access to that information they may avoid the development of sites where rare species of plants and animals occur. Ecologists may use information in the design of ecological restoration projects. Land owners also may use information about species distributions in the design of farm management plans to identify areas most suitable for soil and water conservation. Scientists may be able to use the information that is available to provide ecological explanations for observed distribution patterns. However, access to information about the distribution of some species may have disadvantages. For example, information about the distribution of rare or threatened species may be used by people wanting to collect those species and as a result populations may become extinct. Populations of some species may be destroyed simply as a result of people visiting the site where the species occur, particularly those species that survive in fragile environments. [P02] Philosophical and historical research are the best examples of the confusion from which we suffer as to what constitutes research in the first place. In one sense research is an activity—the basic activity of science. Is philosophy science? Is history science? University philosophy and history departments are not included among the science departments in that philosophical and historical scholarship are considered to be essential in the humanities or social studies. Yet there are "Arts and Sciences" divisions that include them, even if, strictly speaking, they are neither art nor science. I have no particular interest in this confusion except that it makes apparent the association of the word "science" with the classical Newtonian assumptions that the universe is completely objective; science therefore is and must be completely objective; and anything not completely objective is, ipso facto, not science. Those assumptions are no longer valid even in the so-called hard sciences. While it may take several generations for these conceptual dilemmas to be worked out, we can begin to move in the direction of solutions by being more flexible in our definition of science. We should recognize that if scientific method is strictly conceived as being limited to experiments it is exemplary of the total scientific endeavor only under the narrowest, most regressive point of view. The experiment itself has been so thoroughly reassessed that we are no longer sure how to use it. So it would seem reasonable to conceive science as an endeavor, carried out in a great variety of ways, to achieve conceptual clarity about ourselves and our world. That permits philosophy and history to be part of the endeavor while also honoring the distinctions between science and those fields clearly not science, such as art and religion.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 과학을 하나의 활동(endeavor)으로 볼 때 궁극적으로 성취하고자 하는 바를 가리키는 표현을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (2단어, 영어로)

det.korean: 본문: to conceive science as an endeavor ... to achieve conceptual clarity about ourselves and our world — 개념적 명료함(conceptual clarity)
det.analysis: 본문 'it would seem reasonable to conceive science as an endeavor, carried out in a great variety of ways, to achieve conceptual clarity about ourselves and our world' — 과학이라는 활동이 궁극적으로 성취하려는 바 = conceptual clarity(개념적 명료함)
det.tip: conceptual clarity = 개념적 명료함. 과학 활동의 궁극적 목표.

questions.passage: We should recognize that if scientific method is strictly __________ (conceive) as being limited to experiments it is exemplary of the total scientific endeavor only under the narrowest, most regressive point of view.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: conceive → conceived: 'be동사(is) + 과거분사'의 수동태. 과학적 방법이 '여겨지는' 대상이므로 수동
det.analysis: conceive(동사) → conceived(과거분사). 'if scientific method is strictly conceived as being limited to experiments' — be동사 is 뒤 수동태 자리. 과학적 방법이 '~라고 여겨지는' 대상이므로 수동의 과거분사 conceived. is conceived as ~로 '~라고 간주되다' 구문
det.tip: be conceived as = ~라고 여겨지다(수동). conceive → conceived.

questions.stem: 윗글 전반부(종 분포 정보에 관한 글)의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ④ 정보 공개의 장단점(정답). 전반부 전체가 공개의 장점(계획·복원·보존 활용)과 단점(수집 악용·멸종)을 다룸
det.analysis:
❌ ① 생태 복원 절차: 복원은 정보 활용의 한 예시일 뿐, 절차를 설명하지 않음

❌ ② 희귀종 수집 방법: 수집은 단점의 사례로만 언급, 글의 주제 아님

❌ ③ 데이터베이스의 기술적 한계: 접근성 증대의 맥락일 뿐 기술적 한계가 주제 아님

✅ ④ 정보 공개의 장점과 단점: 'There are advantages and disadvantages in making information ... openly available' — 전반부 전체가 공개의 양면을 다룸 ← 정답
det.tip: advantages and disadvantages = 장단점. 전반부의 핵심 축.

ch: 생태 복원 프로젝트를 설계하는 구체적 절차
종 분포 정보를 공개하는 것의 장점과 단점

questions.stem: 윗글 후반부(과학의 정의에 관한 글)의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ③ 정의를 유연하게 하면 철학·역사도 포함 가능(정답). 글의 결론
det.analysis:
❌ ① 철학·역사는 결코 과학이 될 수 없다: 필자는 오히려 포함 가능성을 열어둠. 반대

❌ ② 완전한 객관성 전제: 본문은 그 가정이 'no longer valid'라고 함. 반대

✅ ③ 정의를 유연하게 하면 포함 가능: 'we can begin to move in the direction of solutions by being more flexible in our definition of science ... to conceive science as an endeavor, carried out in a great variety of ways' — 정의를 넓히면 철학·역사도 탐구에 포함 ← 정답

❌ ④ 실험이 유일한 기준: 본문은 실험에 국한하는 것을 '가장 퇴행적 관점'이라 비판. 반대
det.tip: more flexible in our definition of science = 과학의 정의를 더 유연하게. 포함의 논리.

ch: 철학과 역사는 결코 과학의 일부가 될 수 없다.
과학은 완전한 객관성을 전제로 할 때만 성립한다.
과학의 정의를 더 유연하게 하면 철학·역사도 과학적 탐구에 포함될 수 있다.
실험은 과학적 방법의 유일하고 확실한 기준이다.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말을 [조건]에 맞게 영작하시오. (영어로)
우리말: 종 분포에 관한 정보를 공개적으로 이용 가능하게 만드는 데에는 장점과 단점이 있다.
[조건] (1) about, advantages, and, are, available, disadvantages, distributions, in, information, making, openly, species, There를 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 13단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: There are advantages and disadvantages(장점과 단점이 있다) in making information about species distributions(종 분포에 관한 정보를 만드는 데에) openly available(공개적으로 이용 가능하게)
det.analysis: 구문: There are + 주어(advantages and disadvantages) + in + 동명사구(making information ... openly available). 'make + 목적어(information about species distributions) + 목적격보어(openly available)' 구조가 동명사 making에 담김. There is/are 구문 + 전치사 in + 동명사
det.tip: There are A and B in making O C = O를 C하게 만드는 데에 A와 B가 있다. make + O + 형용사(보어).
